text:
olivia (Helios): Hey team — starting ~2026-03-17T09:05UTC we saw a campaign-triggered spike from our helios-prod dedicated pool. Baseline ~50 RPS, peak ~420 RPS for ~8m. P95 latency jumped to ~920ms and ~2% requests returned 429. We're on min_nodes=4, max_nodes=12, target_util=0.6. Any quick mitigation?

maria (Support): Thanks — looking now. Can you paste the pool name, example request ids and the exact campaign start time? Any recent config changes or batch jobs around 09:00? :eyes:

olivia (Helios): Pool: helios-prod-pool-1. Example req ids: r_0a3f12, r_0a3f13, r_0a3f98. Campaign kicked at 09:05:12 UTC. No manual config changes from our side. We did kick off a nightly bulk-embed job at 09:03 to precompute embeddings for the campaign recipients (size=2000). Billing alerts from our side also flagged increased spend during the window.

autoscale-bot: autoscaler event: pool=helios-prod-pool-1 scale_up_start=1898765460 requested_delta=2 current_nodes=4 max_nodes=12 cooldown=120s

sanjay (SRE): I can see the pool metrics. Quick summary: autoscaler started scaling at ~09:06 but only added nodes slowly because scale_up_cooldown=120s and concurrent-scaling limit is 1. Meanwhile a background job (bulk-embed) was consuming a large fraction of GPU cycles causing queueing and higher tail latency. Logs excerpt:

```
[09:04:12] job=bulk-embed id=be_332 queued=2000 batch_size=256 op=embed start
[09:04:15] pool=helios-prod-pool-1 node=10.2.1.9 load=0.68 gpu_util=0.73
[09:04:18] queue_length=1800 gpu_wait_ms=1420 p95_latency_ms=310
[09:05:30] user_requests_inflight=480 user_queue=300 throttled=12 error=429
```

maria (Support): So two contributors: noisy neighbor (bulk job) + autoscaler slow to add headroom. For bursty campaigns we want faster scale-up or reserved headroom. Immediate mitigations I can do with you: 1) enable temporary burst nodes (ephemeral GPUs) for 15m; 2) bump min_nodes to 6; 3) lower target_util to 0.5 so autoscaler keeps more headroom. Which do you want to try first?

olivia (Helios): Please enable burst nodes and lower target_util to 0.5. Also we'll pause the bulk-embed job.

maria (Support): On it — enabling burst + patching autoscale policy now. API calls I used (example):

```
# enable burst
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/pools/helios-prod-pool-1/operations/enable-burst \
  -d '{"duration_minutes":15,"max_extra_nodes":4}'

# patch autoscale
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/pools/helios-prod-pool-1 \
  -d '{"autoscale": {"min_nodes":6,"target_utilization":0.5,"scale_up_cooldown":30}}'
```

maria (Support): Done. autoscale-bot: burst_enabled, autoscale updated.

autoscale-bot: pool=helios-prod-pool-1 burst=ON extra_nodes=3 new_min_nodes=6 target_util=0.5 scale_up_cooldown=30

sanjay (SRE): After changes we should see queue shrink and p95 drop. For post-incident: recommended longer-term changes:
- Set min_nodes to at least 25% of expected peak for known campaigns (Helios peak ~420 RPS → keep min_nodes=ceil(0.25*peak_capacity)).
- For highly bursty traffic set target_util between 0.45–0.6 and reduce scale_up_cooldown to 20–30s.
- Add a rate-limited admission control for internal batch jobs so they don't compete with user traffic.

lucas (Customer Success): For planning, can you translate peak RPS -> node count estimate? Olivia, fill in avg tokens per request and model variant.

olivia (Helios): avg tokens ~60, model=redwood-2-small, perf ≈ 80 requests/sec per GPU at that token size (measured).

sanjay (SRE): Quick calc: at 80 RPS/GPU, peak 420 RPS needs ~6 GPUs sustained. With target_util=0.5 you need ~12 GPUs headroom to keep latency low (420 / (80*0.5) ≈ 10.5 → round to 11–12). Current max_nodes=12 was borderline; because autoscaler lag + noisy job we hit throttles. Recommendation: set max_nodes to 16 for campaigns, and schedule a reserved burst window.

olivia (Helios): That makes sense. Can we add a runbook to avoid this in the future and a reproducible test to validate autoscale?

maria (Support): Yes. Runbook (short):
1) Before campaign: set min_nodes = max(ceil(0.25*expected_peak_nodes), 6) and enable burst with max_extra_nodes=ceil(0.2*expected_peak_nodes).
2) Pause/queue internal batch jobs or tag them as low priority (admission control).
3) Deploy autoscale policy: target_util=0.5 scale_up_cooldown=30 scale_down_cooldown=300 max_nodes=expected_peak_nodes*1.2.
4) Monitor: watch p95_latency, user_queue_length, throttle_rate, and GPU_util.

Repro steps (dev/staging):
# use wrk to simulate user+batch mix
wrk -t12 -c400 -d5m --script=campaign_ramp.lua http://staging.helios.internal/generate

campaign_ramp.lua (pseudo): ramp from 50 RPS to 420 RPS over 90s, hold 10m, mix 5% long-batch requests.

maria (Support): I'll attach these changes to your account and we can run the staging repro together. After the immediate fix p95 dropped from ~920ms → ~160ms and 429s went to 0 in the next 3m.

olivia (Helios): Great, thanks. Follow-up: we'd like a permanent autoscale tuning session and a recording of the repro run. Also can you confirm whether the bulk-embed run incurred extra billable usage?

lucas (Customer Success): We'll open a billing review ticket for the bulk job charges and see if credits apply; I'll own that.

sanjay (SRE): I'll draft a short postmortem with timeline and the config diffs. Action items: 1) Helios pauses heavy batch jobs during campaigns (customer). 2) Support/SRE update autoscale policy and enable campaign reservations (support). 3) CS open billing review (CS).

maria (Support): Closing loop for now — monitoring shows healthy metrics. Reopen if throttles reappear. :white_check_mark:
